exposure: Imported feed protein concentrated on the Americas
protein_food_affected: Pork, poultry, eggs, milk, farmed fish
evidence_of_exposure: Soybeans 95.4% from three origins in 2023 (Brazil 50.1%, United States 38.5%); soybean meal 88.9% (Argentina 51.3%); maize 89.1%; HHI 3,149 to 4,053; about 99% of feed soy protein imported
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: Only through domestic-input routes. Net saving at D-BENCH 2035: minus 0.2 to 5.6 kt of soy protein for a soy-based substitute; 4.5 to 8.0 kt for a domestic-input substitute; at most 0.24% of 3,312 kt soybean-meal protein fed (2025)
notes: Shares and HHI our calculation from Vietnam-reported 2023 data; net saving our calculation (sec_calc.py) from balance-model assumptions (Low).

exposure: Imported food plant-protein ingredients concentrated on China
protein_food_affected: Chay foods, processed meat extenders, plant milks
evidence_of_exposure: China about 84% of 2025 tonnage of HS 3504, 2106.10 and 1109 reaching Vietnam (53,976 of 64,248 t, partner-reported); gluten 59.3% China by 2023 value
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: No. Alternative protein made from these ingredients adds to the China dependence. Local textured soy on imported flour moves the origin, not the dependence
notes: Our calculation from ch16 partner-reported tonnages.

protein_food_affected: Tofu, soy milk, soy foods; wheat noodles and bread
evidence_of_exposure: Soy foods 4.94 g and wheat 3.27 g of 102.2 g protein per person per day (2023), about 8% of supply and about 305 kt of protein a year at 101.6 million people; soybeans 98.4% and wheat 100% imported
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: No. The incumbent alternative protein (tofu, soy milk) is part of this exposure; more soy food from imported beans enlarges it
notes: FBS supply, not intake; tonnage our calculation. L4 covers the full food balance.

protein_food_affected: Mung bean in chay fillings and sweets
evidence_of_exposure: Dried pulses (HS 0713) 60.2% from Myanmar by 2023 value; mung and black gram 65% from Myanmar (2023, FORM-08); domestic mung output not established
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: No. Mung-bean protein products move dependence to Myanmar unless domestic output is established

protein_food_affected: Marine fish eaten fresh, dried and as fish sauce
evidence_of_exposure: Marine standing stock about 3.95 Mt (2016 to 2020), minus 22.1% on 2000 to 2005; capture rose 3.26 Mt (2016) to 3.83 Mt (2024); policy target 2.8 Mt by 2030 (about minus 27% on 2025); fish 25.7% of animal protein supply (2023)
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: No, at the study's scale: food routes displace meat and chay, not fish; no Vietnamese evidence of demand for fish analogues
notes: Share of capture fish in domestic consumption not found (open question).

evidence_of_exposure: Catch potential in Viet Nam's EEZ by 2050 relative to 2000: minus 6.8% (RCP2.6) and minus 11.7% (RCP8.5) in DBEM; minus 2.8% and minus 4.3% in a size-based food-web model; by 2100 under RCP8.5 minus 40.8% against minus 6.5%
notes: Published model results for Viet Nam's EEZ; FAO averages across climate models with wide ranges. Two fisheries models disagree; not averaged (see disagreements).

protein_food_affected: Farmed pangasius, tilapia, shrimp, other farmed fish
evidence_of_exposure: FAO ranks Viet Nam the most vulnerable country for freshwater aquaculture and high for brackish-water; about 1.1 Mt of output (USD 935 million) at annual flood risk; 8,715 ha of aquaculture damaged by salinity in 2019 to 2020
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: No material difference at about 0.2% of meat protein displaced in 2035
notes: Flood and salinity figures already in the package (CI-13, CI-24).

exposure: Heat in livestock becoming a power-reliability exposure
evidence_of_exposure: Livestock department advice (June 2026) to secure power and water against heat, especially for large farms; press headline of 700 pigs dead after a night power cut in Bac Ninh (snippet only); heat-stress days rising (CLM-22)
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: Shifts rather than removes: fermentation plants also need continuous power and chilled water. No per-kg comparison found

exposure: Consumer protein-price shocks from domestic disease
evidence_of_exposure: Pork prices +57.23% in 2020 (1.94 points of a 3.23% CPI rise); processed meat +21.59%; foods +12.28%
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: No, at the study's scale (about 19 kt of protein delivered in 2035 against about 0.93 Mt of meat protein supply); consumers switched to chicken, not tofu, in 2019 to 2020

protein_food_affected: All livestock and aquaculture products (via farm margins)
evidence_of_exposure: 2022: wheat import price +37%, yet consumer foods +1.62%, pork minus 10.68%, chicken +4.29%, beef +0.8%; 2026: feed +10 to 14% while farm-gate egg prices fell below cost, and consumer food and food services rose 4.76% (January to August) with no item breakdown
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: Not for consumers; import-based food routes carry the same soy-complex price risk. Domestic-input routes would hedge processors, not households
notes: Shocks land mainly on farmers and processors (smallholder exit, SHK-009); 2026 consumer pass-through not separable from energy and the 2025 ASF wave.

evidence_of_exposure: 2008: CPI +22.97%; staples more than 49%; other foods more than 32%
notes: Press report of GSO data; no meat breakdown.

protein_food_affected: Indirect, through feed and freight costs
evidence_of_exposure: 2024 Red Sea: container rates to US East Coast +58 to 73% (Dec 2023 to Jan 2024), not shown to affect soy or maize imports; over a quarter of world soybean exports transit Malacca (2017 analysis); 2026 Middle East shock via energy, fertiliser and freight
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: Only domestic-input routes reduce it; import-based food routes from China use shorter routes, changing but not removing route risk
notes: Route risk for protein inputs is our reading.

protein_food_affected: Soy, soybean meal, maize; food protein ingredients
evidence_of_exposure: Argentina raised meal export duties in 2022 and is cutting them to 2028; domestic inflation predicts export restrictions; China lists import diversification as a 2026 task; no Chinese export control on protein ingredients found
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: Import-based routes keep this exposure (origin changes); domestic-input routes reduce it
notes: We found no export restriction on Chinese soy isolate, gluten or textured protein; not a finding of absence.

exposure: Dairy shortfall against the food-security target
evidence_of_exposure: Resolution 34 targets 2.6 Mt of fresh milk by 2030; output 1.3 Mt (2025), 1.37 Mt planned for 2026 (about 53%)
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: Possibly, in principle: precision-fermented dairy proteins on domestic sugar; strains and patents imported; no Vietnamese evidence
notes: Dairy import volumes and origins: line L1.

exposure: Food-security policy frame without an import or protein indicator
evidence_of_exposure: Resolution 34/NQ-CP (2021 to 2030) sets volume targets and asks for more meat, milk, eggs and fish; imports only a 'flexible' management tool; MAE 2026 plan adds 'reduce import dependence by developing domestic raw-material areas' for livestock
does_alt_protein_for_food_reduce_it: Not applicable; the frame decides whether domestic-input protein counts as security
